newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share index touch down on Lever Bros.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share index touch down on Lever Bros.

text.p: Shares of Lever Brothers Plc, one of the most capitalised on the Nigerian stock exchange, fell in Thursday's trading, dragging down the all-share index with it.
The index closed at 6997.82 from Wednesday's 6997.83 despite positive movements by some other blue chips, traders said.
The conglomerate's shares fell on profit-taking but other losses were due to poor corporate performance or excess shares.
Among these were Ashaka Cement, down five kobo to 16.20 naira and Guaranty Trust Bank, 10 kobo lower at 10.80 naira.
Textiles group Afprint lost five kobo to 2.60 naira as traders reacted to a fire that destroyed the warehouse of its subsidiary with the loss of goods valued at 237 milliona naira.
This was in spite of a company statement on Thursday saying the fire would not affect its financial results.
Nigerian Bottling Company rose by 50 kobo to 30.00 naira on better third-quarter result released on the trading floor.
It said after-tax profit to-end-September 1996 shot to 902 million naira against 753 million naira to end-September 1995.
Fellow food sector firm Nestle rose on investors' positive perception to 50.50 naira, up 50 kobo.
West African Portland Cement Company also soared 35 kobo to 47.50 naira on strong demand.
The market's capitalisation got a boost with the listing of 139 million Guinness shares which the foreign partner in the company converted to equities late last year.
The value of the shares was put at some 426.8 million naira, raising Guinness Nigeria's market capitalisation to 5.5 billion naira from 4.3 billion naira before the listing.
Guinness shares closed unchanged at 8.16 naira. ($1=80 naira)
